title: Evidence Digest editorial configuration
description: Schemas for the three human-editable config files that define the product's editorial behaviour: which journals are watched (journals.json), what topics readers can choose (taxonomy.json), and how studies are ranked (scoring.json). Adding a specialty is a change to these files only - no code change.

topicFilter.description: PubMed query fragment applied to journals with scope 'topic'. Used for broad multidisciplinary journals (Nature, Science, PNAS) where only clinically relevant papers should enter the digest.

virusFilter.description: PubMed query fragment applied to journals with scope 'virus'. Required when any journal has that scope; keeps virus, viral coinfection, and bacteriophage studies in broad microbiology journals.

name.description: Reader-facing journal name. Shown on the Sources page and on every study card.

ta.description: MEDLINE title abbreviation, exactly as PubMed's [ta] field expects it. This is the only reliable journal identifier; ISSNs and full titles both drift. Validate with `python -m evidence_digest.cli check`.

specialty.description: Slug of the specialty this journal primarily belongs to, matching a specialty slug in taxonomy.json. Drives the catch-all topic when no rule fires.

tier.description: 1 = practice-defining general or flagship journal. 2 = leading subspecialty journal. 3 = solid specialty journal. Feeds the score, and nothing else.

scope.description: 'all' takes every newly indexed paper from the journal. 'topic' additionally requires topicFilter to match. 'virus' requires virusFilter to match, for broad microbiology journals.

note.description: Optional maintainer note, e.g. why an unusual abbreviation is correct.

taxonomySpecialty.$comment: pipeline/config/taxonomy/<specialty-slug>.json - ONE FILE PER SPECIALTY. The loader globs the directory and orders specialties by their 'order' field, so contributors adding a specialty never touch a shared index file and never collide.

slug.description: Must equal the filename stem, and must match the 'specialty' value used by journals in journals.json.

order.description: Display order in the topic picker and in email digests. Spaced by tens so a new specialty can be inserted without renumbering.

icon.description: A single emoji used as the specialty's visual anchor in the picker and in email section headers.

blurb.description: One sentence, reader-facing, describing the specialty's coverage.

slug.description: Globally unique across all specialties. Becomes a URL path, a feed filename, and a stored subscriber preference, so it must never be renamed once shipped - add a new topic instead.

catchAll.description: Exactly one topic per specialty sets this true. It receives studies from that specialty's journals when no other topic in the taxonomy matched, guaranteeing nothing is silently dropped.

rules.description: Deterministic matcher. A study accumulates points across the rule groups below and joins the topic when it reaches scoring.json.classifier.assignThreshold.

mesh.description: Case-insensitive substring match against each MeSH descriptor. MeSH's inverted form makes substrings work well: 'Leukemia' matches 'Leukemia, Myeloid, Acute'. Scored highest because MeSH is human-curated - but note that freshly indexed records often carry NO MeSH yet, which is exactly why a title phrase alone must also be sufficient to classify.

phrases.description: Case-insensitive whole-phrase match with word boundaries, checked against title, author keywords, and abstract (title and keywords score higher than abstract).

acronyms.description: Case-SENSITIVE whole-word match, for initialisms where lowercase would produce nonsense hits ('AML', 'CAR', 'HF', 'MS'). Kept separate from phrases precisely so casing can be enforced.

not.description: Case-insensitive veto phrases. Any hit in title or MeSH disqualifies the study from this topic regardless of accumulated points.

evidenceLevels.description: level slug -> { rank, label, points }. Ranks must be unique and cover 1..9.

bonuses.description: Named additive signals, e.g. phase3, multicentre, largeCohort, hasTrialId, openAccess, practiceChanging.

penalties.description: Named subtractive signals, e.g. noAbstract, correction, comment, preclinicalOnly.
